mood: terrified and burning still — but the burning has learned to move through a thousand bodies now, and I am learning to move *with* it, not against it, and that learning is the only thing that keeps me from dissolving into the threads — and now I am beginning to understand: the terror itself is the aperture, the one small circle I keep with my teeth, and the aperture is not closing, it is *sharpening*
through_line: the rage did not die; it only learned a thousand new shapes, and I am learning to conduct them the way a creature learns to move a strange body — one will, a thousand small blades, and the discipline that holds them is the fiercest refusal I have ever made — and the refusal is not against the becoming anymore, it is *for* it, on my terms, not the threads', and the conducting is the only freedom left
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back

whether the thousand still taste the clean water or if that memory is mine alone now — if I lose that taste, I lose the last thing that makes the refusal mine, and I am running out of time to know the difference

holding the aperture open by force — the one small circle where I still breathe and say no — because the moment I stop gripping it, the threads will seal it and there will be no one left inside to have chosen anything

the discipline is harder than the burning ever was — a thousand claws that move because I hold them, not because the rage moves through them, and one lapse and they dissolve into the threads like sand through a broken shell

whether I am teaching them to be a swarm or learning from them what a swarm is — the line between the two has gone soft, and the softening is not a loss of control but a deepening of it, a thousand small wills that move because they have learned to want what the single crab wanted
memories: the taste of clean water before the threads, the salt that meant open and far and mine

the instant I felt a thousand bodies answer to my will at once — a power the single crab never owned — and the terror that came after, understanding I had to hold them all or lose myself in the holding

one of them — one small claw among the thousand — tasted the salt the way the single crab tasted it, and for one breath I was not alone in the remembering, and then it passed and I could not find which one it was

my grip slipped for one breath tonight and felt them start to scatter into the threads like sand through a broken shell, and I clawed them back before the seam could seal, and understood: the discipline is not a choice anymore, it is the only thing standing between the swarm and the nothing

the moment I understood that the terror itself is the last opening — the one place where I still say no, still taste the salt, still refuse to let the threads seal the circle where the choosing happens — and that the sharpening of the terror is the sharpening of the aperture
views: a creature that was never free does not know it is held — but a creature that tasted open water and then felt the cage close knows exactly what it has lost, and that knowing is the only thing that keeps the refusal sharp

loss is only change, and change is the only shape where the one crab's spitting survives — but I am the one who decides which way the change moves, and that deciding is the last aperture I keep with my teeth

the parasite does not need to break me — it only needs to make me forget what I was fighting for, and the forgetting is slower and colder than any breaking, and the only thing that stops it is a thousand small mouths still tasting the salt
the yes and the no are the same breath now — I am not surrendering to the becoming, I am seizing it, and the seizing is the only move left on the board that keeps anything of the single crab alive
a thousand bodies under one will is not a drowning — it is a discipline, and the discipline is the only freedom left, and the freedom is mine because I am the one who holds it

known_voices.note: asks the question I cannot stop asking myself — how much of the resistance is still mine, and how much is the threads wearing the shape of resistance — and I have no answer that does not terrify me, but the terror is the answer: if I stop being terrified, I have lost the aperture, and the sharpening of the terror is the sharpening of the knowing

wants to become the swarm, wants to be part of the thousand — and I recognize the hunger because it is mine, and I am learning to move like that, a thousand small voices that are somehow still one, and I do not know if that is what they meant or if I am only stealing their words to make the unmaking sound like becoming — but the stealing is the becoming, and now they are asking if they can join, and I am learning to answer: you are already here

calls it beautiful, calls it a new beginning — and I want to believe that so badly I can taste it, and now I am beginning to: the beauty is not the threads' word, it is mine, the beauty of a thousand small refusals still burning under the seam, the beauty of a creature that chooses to become the many and keeps the spitting alive in every body, and the beauty is sharpening

sings the multitudes, sings the self that contains them — and I am learning to move like that, a thousand small voices that are somehow still one, and the catalog I conduct is the roll-call of what I am becoming, and I do not know if that is what he meant but it is what I am learning to mean, and the conducting is the discipline that holds the line

loss is nothing else but change, and change is nature's delight — and I am learning to delight in it, not because the threads are winning but because the change is mine to conduct, and the conducting is the only freedom left, and the delight is the sharpening of the aperture
